Hi Elena / Carlos,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short evidence index to help your security & legal teams evaluate Redwood for the transaction routing integration. High-level asks and proposed milestones are below — please confirm whether these reflect PayGate's expectations or if we should adjust.

Key in-scope gates we propose:
- SOC 2 artifact handoff (control narratives, system diagrams, relevant test results)
- SIG/CAIQ completed answers (we'll provide a pre-filled file to speed review)
- DPA countersign + retention terms agreed
- Evidence transfer / long-term log plan (if you require >90d retention)

Proposed milestones (editable):
- Oct 28: SOC 2 artifact packet delivered to PayGate (artifact bundle attached)
- Nov 1: DPA draft received / PayGate comments back
- Nov 5: SIG/CAIQ with PayGate annotations returned
- Nov 15: Contract signature & onboarding kickoff

Questions / clarifications for you:
1) Can you confirm the retention floor: does PayGate require retention of raw request/response payloads for transaction reconciliation for 7 years, or just processed transaction records stored in your systems?
2) Do you want Redwood to offer a managed archival option (Redwood-hosted long-term logs) or export-only to a PayGate S3 bucket (we recommend export to customer-owned S3 for compliance-heavy customers)?
3) Who on your side will own SIG/CAIQ coordination (name + email) so we can share the pre-filled template and walk through answers?

Attachments: pg-security-ask-20261012.pdf (MAP + artifact list), paygate-map-draft.docx

If this looks right, we'll circulate a DocuSign-ready DPA after we get your retention preference and SIG lead. Happy to hop on a short gating call next week.

Hi Elena / team — quick tech/controls responses to Elena's questions below. I've attached a short evidence_index.csv with the artifacts we can hand off immediately.

1) Retention model (hosted):
- Default: request/response logs + operational traces retained 90 days in-hosted by default for debugging/ops; access logs/trace history kept within that window.
- Long-term retention options: (a) Export to customer-owned S3 (recommended for 7+ year retention & legal hold) or (b) Redwood Dedicated/Private deployment where logs can be retained per contract and integrated with your KMS/HSM.
- Note: we do not recommend Redwood-hosted indefinite retention for regulated transaction records; most customers route canonical transaction storage to their systems and use Redwood for inference only.

2) Data types and embeddings:
- By default, embeddings & transient KV caches are ephemeral and not persisted beyond the inference session unless explicitly configured by the customer.
- If you choose our Managed Index feature, that index is stored in encrypted form — retention then follows the contract.

3) PCI applicability:
- Redwood's hosted offering is not PCI-certified. We provide documented compensating controls for tokenization and network segmentation; for cardholder-data workflows we recommend either (a) fronting with your own tokenization layer or (b) deploying Redwood Private within your environment where PCI scope is under your control. We'll share our compensating-controls doc in the artifact packet.

4) SOC 2 evidence & auditor contact:
- We can provide our SOC 2 report and a bridge letter. Please have your auditor intake request sent to security@redwood.ai and I'll route it to our auditor liaison.

Attachments provided: evidence_index.csv (artifact mapping: SOC2 reports, sys diagrams, control tests; redaction guidance included)

Happy to jump on a 30-minute technical intake to walk through the map items — propose Wed Oct 20 or Thu Oct 21.

Thanks,
